Noted, not held against the check (its words are four demonstrations, all shown): (a) the title, evidence and design.md say 'the fewest that fight', but the deletion filter returns one irreducible set (no member can be dropped), not the smallest. With a 2-joint conflict (two hinges 0.02 rad out of line) and a 3-joint conflict (a loop of three fixed joints 0.1 m short) in one set, the joint order decides: given [hinge, hinge, loop...] it named the 3 loop joints; given [loop..., hinge, hinge] it named the 2 hinges. Likewise jB,jA,qa,qb named [jA,qa,qb] where {jA,jB} also fights. Only one conflict is named per connected set; the other waits until the first is fixed. (b) False fights from local minima: in 150 random systems that are consistent by construction (random kinds, trees plus up to 2 extra loop joints, random given poses), 2 stopped at a local minimum (t21 planar/planar/cylindrical/ball, t40 cylindrical/revolute/cylindrical) and were reported as fighting with joints named, though started from the true poses the same joints hold with fight null. Start strategy is the likely cause; the joints named in such a case do not fight. (c) A ball joint, which holds only a point, is reported as flipped when its two frames' n happen to point the same way in the given pose (ball with identical n at identity pose: flipped ['B']); n has no meaning for a ball. (d) The evidence's own 'Not done' (rigid clusters not split out; a fit's play is not a range) is stated and is outside the check. Suggest these three go in as faults or follow-up tasks.
